newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Analysts cheer expected Nethold cash boost.
newsitem.headline: Analysts cheer expected Nethold cash boost.

text.p: Talk of a major alliance for pay-TV concern NetHold, possibly involving a $1 billion cash injection by Hughes Electric Corp of the U.S., was cheered by South African analysts on Friday.
Richemont Securities, 50-percent shareholder in the Dutch-based concern with MIH Holdings Ltd, is to make an important announcement after 1400 GMT, expected to involve NetHold.
The Wall Street journal reported earlier that Hughes Electric Corp, a unit of General Motors, was in serious talks to invest as much as $1 billion for a 30-percent stake in NetHold.
Shares in Richemont were suspended in Zurich and Johannesburg earlier on Friday, along with those of MIH and MIH's leading shareholder, Omni Media Corp Ltd.
Analysts said the most likely outcome was for Hughes to inject new funds into the developing business, which has yet to turn a profit.

"If Richemont converts its preference shares, then Richemont will end up with an effective 39 pct, MIH with 33 percent and Hughes with 28 percent," said one equity analyst who asked not to be identified.
"It's good news. Nethold badly needs cash at this stage."
A second analyst agreed: "The key is to keep ahead of the pack -- and that makes it a cash-hungry business."
NetHold has shown impressive growth in its subscriber base, which increased by over 335,000 to some 2.7 million in over 50 countries in the year to March 31, 1996.
That made it the third largest pay-TV operator outside the U.S., according to analysts. But the company had still not been expected to break even much before the turn of the century.
The entry of a cash-rich partner could change that, providing a fillip to its existing shareholders.
Richemont's share of NetHold's operating loss increased by 8.2 million stg to 46.3 million in the 1995/96 financial year.
The Wall Street Journal said NetHold was one of two satellite deals being pursued by Hughes which, if completed, would make it a global force in satellite broadcasting.

Hughes is also the leading contender to acquire control of PanAmSat Corp, the world's leading privately held satellite system, in a complex deal that could be valued at as much as $3 billion, the newspaper said.
